t3.texto: Part three. How is soil made?

t4.texto: Part four. The layers of soil.

t10.texto: Part ten. Soil quiz and song.

c1_1.texto: Hello, friends! Welcome to a very special adventure.

c1_2.texto: Look down at the floor, in front of you. Something is moving!

c1_3.texto: Hi there! Hello! Can you see me? I am Wiggles, the earthworm!

c1_4.texto: I live under the ground, in the *soil*. The soil is my home!

c1_5.texto: Wave hello to me! Come on, wave your hand!

c1_7.texto: Today, we are going on a soil adventure! We will learn about different *types of soil*.

c1_9.texto: Can you say soil? Say it with me: soil!

c1_10.texto: Great job! Are you ready? Let’s go!

c2_1.texto: This is *soil*. Soil covers the ground almost everywhere on Earth.

c2_2.texto: Soil looks like dirt. But soil is not just dirt! It is made of many things.

c2_4.texto: First: tiny pieces of *rock*. Big rocks break into very, very small pieces.

c2_5.texto: Next: old leaves and dead plants. They rot and become dark and soft. This is called *humus*.

c2_7.texto: Soil has *water*, too. Plants drink this water with their roots.

c2_8.texto: Soil also has *air*! There are tiny spaces between the pieces, and air lives in those spaces.

c2_9.texto: And soil has *living things*, like me! Worms, ants, beetles, and tiny, tiny helpers called bacteria.

c2_10.texto: Touch each thing to say hello!

c2_11.texto: So, soil is a mix of rock pieces, humus, water, air and living things.

c2_12.texto: Let’s count them with our fingers! Rocks, one. Humus, two. Water, three. Air, four. Living things, five!

c2_13.texto: Soil is very important. Plants grow in soil, and we eat plants!

c2_14.texto: Fruits, vegetables, rice and corn all grow in soil. Yummy!

c2_15.texto: Hmm... But where does soil come from? Let’s find out!

c3_1.texto: Close your eyes... and open them! We are in the mountains.

c3_2.texto: Wow! Look at this big rock. It is very old and very hard.

c3_3.texto: In the day, the sun makes the rock hot.

c3_4.texto: At night, the rock gets cold. Hot, cold, hot, cold. Little cracks appear!

c3_5.texto: Then the rain comes. Water gets into the tiny cracks.

c3_6.texto: When it is very cold, the water turns into ice. The ice pushes, and pushes, and... crack!

c3_7.texto: Plant roots grow into the cracks, too. They push the rock apart.

c3_8.texto: And the wind blows sand against the rock. It rubs, and rubs, and rubs.

c3_9.texto: Now it’s your turn! Tap the rock to help the weather break it!

c3_10.texto: Look! The big rock breaks into small rocks. And the small rocks break into tiny pieces.

c3_11.texto: Leaves fall and rot. Worms and bugs move in. The tiny rock pieces and the humus mix together.

c3_12.texto: And that is how soil is made!

c3_13.texto: But it is very, very slow. It takes hundreds of years to make just a little bit of soil!

c3_14.texto: That is why soil is a treasure. We must take care of it.

c4_1.texto: Now, let’s go down, under the ground! We are on an elevator. Hold on tight!

c4_2.texto: Soil has layers, like a big chocolate cake. Look at the walls around you.

c4_3.texto: This is the top layer. It is called *topsoil*. It is dark and soft.

c4_4.texto: Topsoil has lots of humus. Plant roots, worms and ants live here. This is where I live!

c4_5.texto: Let’s go down a little more.

c4_6.texto: This layer is called *subsoil*. It is lighter in color. It has more rocks and clay.

c4_7.texto: Only big, long roots reach the subsoil, like the roots of trees.

c4_8.texto: And now, all the way to the bottom...

c4_9.texto: This is *bedrock*! It is solid rock. Very, very hard. Soil comes from rock like this.

c4_10.texto: Let’s remember the layers: *topsoil* on top, *subsoil* in the middle, and *bedrock* at the bottom.

c4_11.texto: Quiz time! Which layer has the most living things?

c4_12.texto: The answer is *topsoil*! It has roots, worms and lots of humus.

c4_13.texto: Now, let’s go back up and meet three types of soil!

c5_1.texto: Welcome to the beach! Here we find our first type of soil: *sandy soil*.

c5_2.texto: Sand is made of big pieces of rock. They are called *grains*. Look, I made them really big for you!

c5_3.texto: When you touch sand, it feels *rough* and *dry*. Can you say rough? Rough!

c5_4.texto: Sand grains are big, so there are big spaces between them. Watch the water!

c5_5.texto: Whoosh! The water goes down very fast. Sandy soil does not hold water.

c5_6.texto: Sandy soil dries out quickly, and it has very little humus. Many plants do not like it.

c5_7.texto: But some plants love sandy soil! Like the cactus, and the coconut palm. They do not need a lot of water.

c5_8.texto: Touch the sand grains and make them sparkle!

c5_9.texto: Remember: *sandy soil* is rough, dry, and the water goes through fast!

c6_1.texto: Now we are next to a river. Here we find *clay soil*.

c6_2.texto: Clay is made of tiny, tiny pieces. They are much smaller than sand!

c6_3.texto: When clay is wet, it feels *sticky*. Squish, squish! When clay is dry, it gets very hard.

c6_4.texto: Clay pieces are so small that they stick together. Water cannot go through easily. Watch!

c6_5.texto: Splash! A puddle! Clay soil *holds water*.

c6_6.texto: Some plants, like rice, grow well in wet clay soil.

c6_7.texto: People also use clay to make things: pots, plates, and bricks for houses!

c6_8.texto: Let’s make a pot! Touch the clay!

c6_9.texto: Wow! You made a beautiful pot!

c6_10.texto: Remember: *clay soil* is sticky and smooth, and it holds a lot of water.

c7_1.texto: Our last stop is a farm in the mountains of Ecuador. Here we find *loamy soil*.

c7_2.texto: Loam is my favorite! Loam is a mix of sand, clay, a fine powder called *silt*, and lots of humus.

c7_3.texto: Loam is dark brown. It feels *soft* and crumbly, like cake crumbs!

c7_4.texto: Loam holds *just the right* amount of water and air. Not too much, not too little. Just right!

c7_5.texto: That is why farmers love loamy soil. Most plants grow very well in it.

c7_6.texto: Corn, potatoes, beans, lettuce, and many fruits grow in loam. Yum, yum!

c7_7.texto: Let’s plant some seeds! Touch the little holes to plant them.

c7_8.texto: Look! Your seeds are growing! You are a great farmer!

c7_9.texto: Remember: *loamy soil* is dark, soft, and just right for plants.

c8_1.texto: Now we are back in the classroom. Let’s do a science experiment!

c8_2.texto: Here are three pots. One has *sand*, one has *clay*, and one has *loam*.

c8_3.texto: We will pour the same water into each pot. The water that goes through falls into the glass below.

c8_4.texto: Think! In which pot will the water go through the fastest? Choose one!

c8_6.texto: Look at the sand! The water runs through very fast. The glass is full!

c8_7.texto: The loam lets some water through, but it keeps some for the plants.

c8_8.texto: And the clay? Only a few little drops! Clay holds the water.

c8_9.texto: So: *sand* drains fast, *clay* holds water, and *loam* is just right!

c9_1.texto: Do you know who helps the soil? Me! Worms are *soil helpers*!

c9_2.texto: I dig tunnels. Air and water go into my tunnels.

c9_3.texto: I eat old leaves, and my poop makes the soil healthy. Ha ha!

c9_4.texto: Ants, beetles and tiny bacteria help, too. They turn dead leaves into humus.

c9_5.texto: We can help the soil, too! Here are three ways.

c9_6.texto: One: don’t throw trash on the ground. Help me clean up! Touch the trash to put it in the trash can!

c9_7.texto: Thank you! Clean soil is happy soil!

c9_8.texto: Two: plant trees and plants. Their roots hold the soil, so the rain and the wind cannot take it away.

c9_9.texto: Three: make *compost*! Fruit peels and old leaves can become new humus for the soil.

c10_1.texto: Now, let’s play a game! I describe a soil, and you choose the right one.

c10_2.texto: This soil is rough and dry. The water goes through very fast. Which soil is it?

c10_4.texto: This soil is sticky when it is wet, and it makes puddles. Which soil is it?

c10_6.texto: This soil is dark and soft, and it is just right for plants. Which soil is it?

c10_8.texto: Last one! Which of these is NOT part of soil?

c10_9.texto: *Plastic*! Plastic is trash. It does not belong in the soil.

c10_10.texto: Now, let’s sing the soil song! Repeat after me!

c10_11.texto: Sand is rough, and sand is dry!

c10_12.texto: Clay is sticky, oh my, oh my!

c10_13.texto: Loam is soft, and loam is just right!

c10_14.texto: Take care of soil, day and night!

c10_16.texto: Remember: take care of the soil, and the soil will take care of us.

c10_17.texto: Now I have to go back home. Bye-bye, friends! See you in the garden!

c10_18.texto: The end. Thank you for watching!

c1_11.texto: Here is a tip! When you see a yellow ring, point at it and press the trigger to touch it.

c1_12.texto: Try it now! Touch the three little piles of soil!

c1_13.texto: Great! You know how to play. Now, let’s fly on my magic leaf!

c2_16.texto: Rock pieces make the soil feel rough or smooth. Humus makes it dark and rich. Water and air help the roots drink and breathe.

c5_10.texto: Beach sand comes from rocks and shells. The waves break them into tiny pieces, again and again.

c5_11.texto: Can you say sandy soil? Sandy soil!

c6_11.texto: Can you say clay soil? Clay soil!

c6_12.texto: When clay soil dries in the sun, it cracks. Look at the ground around you!

c7_10.texto: In Ecuador, the volcanoes help, too! Long ago, volcanic ash fell on the land and made the soil very rich.

c7_11.texto: That is why Ecuador grows so many yummy foods: corn, potatoes, beans, bananas, and cacao for chocolate!

c7_12.texto: Can you say loamy soil? Loamy soil!

c9_11.texto: Do you want to know a secret? I have no eyes, no ears and no legs!

c9_12.texto: I breathe through my skin, so I like wet soil. When it rains a lot, I come up to the top!

c10_19.texto: Let’s review what we learned today.

c10_20.texto: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, water, air and living things.

c10_21.texto: Soil has layers: topsoil, subsoil and bedrock.

c10_22.texto: And there are different types of soil: sandy soil, clay soil and loamy soil.
